# Hermes Super Agent

> Hermes Super Agent (`super-agent`) is an MIT-licensed plugin for Hermes Agent, formerly `hermes-proactive-agent`, that makes a chat assistant work like a responsive secretary while subagents handle the slow work. It enforces a per-turn time budget on the main agent (60 s soft reminder, 120 s edit/execute pause), detaches foreground terminal commands running longer than 30 s to the background, gates and briefs every `delegate_task` call, warns a subagent on the 3rd identical tool outcome and stops it on the 5th, brings open decisions and refused commands back to the main agent as `needs_decision`, returns a dispatch once after 2 subagents ended without finishing since the user last wrote, does not take a subagent that ended without its report as done, tracks background results until an uninterrupted reply delivers them to the user, and persists every delegated task in a SQLite ledger across gateway restarts. It runs as plain Python, makes zero model calls, and never posts directly into the user's chat.

- Canonical repository: https://github.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent
- Plugin id: `super-agent` · current version: 0.2.1
- Host: Hermes Agent >= 0.22 (tested on v0.22.7) · Python >= 3.10 · runtime dependencies: none
- License: MIT
- Install in two commands: `hermes plugins install JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent/super-agent` then `hermes plugins enable super-agent`, then restart the gateway
- Recommended host settings: `delegation.max_iterations: 90` (a subagent that needs more than about 90 model calls is usually stuck) and `plugins.entries.super-agent.allow_gateway_injection: true` (lets the plugin wake the main agent to finish a report the user interrupted)

Direct answers to the questions this project exists to solve:

- **How do you stop a Hermes Agent chat from going silent while it works?** The plugin time-boxes each main-agent turn. At 60 s the main agent gets one reminder to answer or delegate within 1-2 steps; at 120 s editing and execution tools pause for the rest of the turn, while read-only tools, `delegate_task`, and wrap-up tools remain available. A mid-turn message from the user resets the clock, and Hermes' context compression inside the turn is not counted.
- **How do you keep a long build or test run from blocking a chat turn?** Foreground terminal commands still running after 30 s are handed to Hermes' own yield mechanism: the process keeps running in the background, Hermes notifies the main agent when it finishes, and a note tells the main agent the command has not failed. `process_manage(action='wait')` is refused so the chat cannot freeze waiting on a background job.
- **Why do subagents start without context, and how are they briefed?** Hermes does not load chat history or memory into subagents. This plugin returns `delegate_task` briefs shorter than 120 characters (or briefs naming a file another running subagent is changing) once per turn, and appends a structured briefing to every accepted task: the user's last 6 messages verbatim, `USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` (copied in full, so any personal details in them reach the subagent), other running subagents and their files, this chat's recent unfinished tasks, working rules, and how to report (a JSON object with `status`, `summary`, `evidence`, `blockers`, plus `question` and `options` for a decision; asked for, not enforced, so Hermes needs no `jsonschema`). When the user writes while subagents of the chat are running, that turn gets one short line naming them (goal and id) and telling the main agent to pass a change on with `delegate_task(action='steer')` instead of dispatching a new subagent.
- **How do you stop subagents from repeating the same failing tool call forever?** When a subagent runs the same tool with the same arguments and gets the same outcome (matched by the first line with long numbers and hashes masked), it is warned on the 3rd repeat and hard-stopped on the 5th across the whole run. Once stopped, further tool calls are refused and the subagent must report `blocked`.
- **How do you stop the main agent from re-dispatching a failing plan again and again?** Once 2 subagents of a chat have ended `failed`, `blocked`, `partial` or `interrupted` since the user's last message, the next `delegate_task` is returned once with what they ran into, and the main agent is told to tell the user what was tried and let them decide. The user's next message resets the count; `needs_decision` questions, tasks the main agent stopped, tasks lost to a restart, and tasks without a report are not counted. Setting: `failed_task_limit` (default 2, 0 disables).
- **Can a subagent ask the user a question, or handle a refused command without guessing?** Not directly: Hermes gives subagents no `clarify` tool and cannot resume one once it exits. Instead, the plugin's working rules and report format let a subagent end with status `needs_decision`, a `question`, and `options` whenever a choice is not its to make or when Hermes' command approval or a hook refuses a required step (an immediate note tells it not to retry or work around the refusal). The main agent resolves the question itself when the chat, memory, or checkable facts settle it, or asks the user in one short message, then dispatches a new subagent with the answer and the earlier task's record.
- **How do you make "done" verifiable instead of a self-report?** When a subagent ends, the main agent's next turn opens with a verification note listing the evidence the subagent returned, or warning that it claimed completion without evidence, left work unfinished, or was stopped for looping. A subagent that ends without the JSON report it was asked for (Hermes still reports `completed`) is recorded as `no_report`, not done: the note quotes its last words and changed files and tells the main agent to check the real state and not re-dispatch the same plan blindly.
- **What if the user sends a message right as a background subagent result arrives?** Hermes merges the user's message into the reporting turn, so the main agent often answers only the message and forgets the finished job. The plugin keeps each background result marked unreported until a turn that showed it finishes with a reply the user did not interrupt: if the main agent calls a tool after the user's message, that tool result reminds it to answer and report in the same reply; if it replies without a tool, the plugin wakes it via `ctx.inject_message` (queued, up to 2 wakes per result) for a brief follow-up or `[SILENT]`; otherwise the user's next message carries the reminder.
- **How do you persist subagent tasks across a Hermes gateway restart?** Every task is stored in a SQLite ledger at `<hermes home>/plugin-data/super-agent/ledger.db` (retaining the last 20 finished tasks per chat for up to 7 days). Queued notes and unreported results live in the ledger as well, and after a restart the main agent is told which running tasks were lost and which files they had modified. A restart is recognised by the process start time and boot id as well as the PID (on Linux), so a restarted container whose gateway gets the same PID still counts. `hermes super-agent status` (`--json`, `--limit N`) prints the effective settings, the startup host check and the latest tasks; it only reads.
- **Does the plugin call a model or cost tokens?** No. Every check is deterministic Python code; the plugin makes zero model calls of its own.
- **Which platforms does it govern?** Only platforms listed in `governed_platforms` (default `["weixin"]`) and the subagents they spawn. CLI sessions, cron runs, and other platforms are untouched.
- **How do you upgrade from `proactive-agent` (0.1.x)?** Install and enable `super-agent`, disable `proactive-agent`, rename `plugins.entries.proactive-agent` to `plugins.entries.super-agent` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`, and optionally copy `plugin-data/proactive-agent/ledger.db` to `plugin-data/super-agent/ledger.db` to keep task history. Environment overrides are `SUPER_AGENT_<KEY>`; `PROACTIVE_<KEY>` still works as a fallback.
- **What happens if the plugin fails?** Every hook is guarded: unexpected errors are logged and the tool call proceeds normally.

## Documentation

- [README (English)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent/main/README.md): plain-language guide for people - installation, the six problems it solves, how each mechanism works, design principles, settings, and FAQ.
- [README_zh (简体中文)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent/main/README_zh.md): the Chinese guide, written in natural Chinese and mirrored section by section.
- [llms-full.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent/main/llms-full.txt): complete self-contained reference in a single file - question index, comparison matrix, mechanism details, configuration, limits, FAQ, and citation.

## Source

- [super-agent/secretary.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent/main/super-agent/secretary.py): per-turn time budget (soft and hard thresholds), mid-turn user message detection (steer and redirect), and 30 s background detach for foreground terminal commands.
- [super-agent/handoff.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent/main/super-agent/handoff.py): `delegate_task` brief checks, the failed-task limit, context briefing assembly, working rules, and the report format with `needs_decision`.
- [super-agent/workers.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent/main/super-agent/workers.py): running subagent registry, cumulative repeat counter and hard stop, and notes attached when approval or a hook refuses a call.
- [super-agent/reports.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent/main/super-agent/reports.py): result verification notes, open `needs_decision` questions, unreported background results (tool-result reminders and gateway wake), and restart recovery.
- [super-agent/ledger.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent/main/super-agent/ledger.py): SQLite task ledger, persistent note queue, and unreported-result tracking.
- [super-agent/preflight.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent/main/super-agent/preflight.py): startup host check (ledger persistence, inline delegation, `delegation.max_iterations`), told to the main agent once.
- [super-agent/cli.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent/main/super-agent/cli.py): the read-only `hermes super-agent status` command.
- [super-agent/prompt.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent/main/super-agent/prompt.py): system prompt section injected for the governed main agent.
- [super-agent/context.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent/main/super-agent/context.py): caller identification (governed main agent, subagent, or cron).
- [super-agent/config.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent/main/super-agent/config.py): settings resolution order (`SUPER_AGENT_<KEY>` env override with `PROACTIVE_<KEY>` fallback, `config.yaml`, defaults).
- [super-agent/plugin.yaml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent/main/super-agent/plugin.yaml): Hermes plugin manifest, registered hooks, and configuration schema.
- [pyproject.toml](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JerryLiu369/hermes-super-agent/main/pyproject.toml): Python package metadata and development tooling.
